intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Jordan strikes militants in Syria
items.text: Jordan's air force has struck what it called terrorist groups in Syria after a deadly attack on a church. Gunmen killed nine people at a funeral at St George's Church in Karak on Friday. Syrian officials said seven people died in the Jordanian strikes, six of them in Daraa province. Three Jordanian men were arrested after they fired on security forces from an abandoned house. King Abdullah II has promised that the attackers will be punished, and the government has declared three days of national mourning.

gloss.air force: the part of the army that fights with aircraft
gloss.funeral: a ceremony held when a dead person is buried
gloss.barricade: to block a door or entrance so that people cannot get in
gloss.retaliation: an attack made in answer to an earlier attack
gloss.national mourning: an official period when a whole country shows sadness for people who died

items.title: Israelis vote in key election
items.text: Israelis are voting today in an election that will decide the future of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. About 7.3 million people are eligible to vote. More than half a million of them are young people voting for the first time. Dawn describes the election as pivotal, because the result will show whether Netanyahu can stay in power. Official results are expected after the polls close.

gloss.eligible: allowed to do something because you meet the rules
gloss.pivotal: very important because everything else depends on it
gloss.stay in power: to keep control of a government
gloss.first-time voter: a person who votes in an election for the first time
gloss.tension: a feeling of worry and anger between groups or countries

items.title: Comey faces third prosecution attempt
items.text: Former FBI director James Comey is facing a third attempt to prosecute him. The Justice Department under President Donald Trump has accused him of transmitting national defence information. It has also accused him of conspiring to transmit it. The case is the latest step in a long legal fight between Comey and the administration. Comey has not yet been shown to have broken the law, and the charges must still be tested in court.

gloss.prosecute: to take someone to court for a crime
gloss.conspire: to secretly plan with others to do something illegal
gloss.defence information: secret facts that protect a country's security
gloss.administration: the government led by a president
gloss.charge: a formal claim that someone has committed a crime

items.title: Kane wins the Ballon d'Or
items.text: Harry Kane has won the men's Ballon d'Or at a ceremony in London. He is the first English winner for 25 years, since Michael Owen in 2001. Kylian Mbappe finished second and Lamine Yamal third. Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last season. Alexia Putellas won the women's award for the third time, and Bukayo Saka received the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work.

gloss.ceremony: a formal event held to mark something special
gloss.humanitarian: connected with helping people who are suffering
gloss.finish second: to come in second place in a competition
gloss.shortlist: a short list of the best candidates, chosen from a longer list
gloss.for club and country: for a team you play for and for your national team

items.title: Alcaraz returns to Vienna
items.text: Carlos Alcaraz plays his first match at the Vienna Open today for the first time since 2021. He added the event after the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh was postponed, and he received a late wild card. Alcaraz is a seven-time Major champion and the second seed. He faces Karen Khachanov, whom he has beaten in all six of their meetings. Jannik Sinner, who won in Vienna in 2023 and 2025, has withdrawn.

gloss.wild card: a special entry that lets a player take part without qualifying
gloss.postpone: to move an event to a later time
gloss.seed: a player ranked high enough to be kept apart from other top players in the draw
gloss.withdraw: to decide not to take part
gloss.Major: one of the four biggest tennis tournaments

items.title: PlayStation Pulse launches with GTA VI
items.text: Sony will release a new wireless headset, the PlayStation Pulse, on 19 November, the same day Grand Theft Auto VI launches. Pre-orders open on 29 October, and it costs £89.99. The headset has planar magnetic drivers and PlayStation Link connectivity. Rockstar and PlayStation are promoting the PS5 as the home of the game, which is optimised for the PS5 Pro. A more expensive headset, the Pulse Edge, is due in 2027.

gloss.pre-order: to pay for a product before it goes on sale
gloss.optimised: made to work as well as possible on a particular device
gloss.launch: to put a new product on sale
gloss.due: expected to happen or arrive at a certain time
gloss.connectivity: the ability to connect to other devices

items.title: Liquid stops tooth decay without drilling
items.text: A large US trial has found that a liquid painted on teeth can stop decay in children without drilling. The trial tested silver diamine fluoride on 830 children younger than six. The treatment stopped decay in more than half of the affected baby teeth when it was applied every six months. It needs no injections or sedation. However, it permanently darkens the treated decay, which may be noticeable on front teeth. The results appeared in JAMA Pediatrics.

gloss.trial: a scientific test to find out whether a treatment works
gloss.decay: the slow damage of a tooth by bacteria
gloss.sedation: medicine that makes a patient calm or sleepy
gloss.drilling: making a hole with a power tool

items.title: Star Trek actor Walter Koenig dies at 90
items.text: Walter Koenig, the actor who played Pavel Chekov in Star Trek, has died at the age of 90. His talent agent said he died at his home in Los Angeles. Koenig played the young Russian officer on the original television series in the 1960s. Chekov became one of the best-known members of the starship's crew, and the character was later played by other actors in new Star Trek films.

gloss.talent agent: a person who finds work for actors and speaks for them
gloss.original series: the first version of a television programme
gloss.crew: all the people who work on a ship or spacecraft
gloss.later: after the time you are talking about

items.title: Oil stays near six-month highs
items.text: Oil prices have stayed close to their highest level for six months. Brent crude settled more than $3 higher and recorded a weekly gain of 6 per cent. US benchmark WTI rose 2.3 per cent. Higher fuel costs are already being felt elsewhere. In Pakistan, for example, the government has blamed the closure of the border with Iran for rising prices of liquefied petroleum gas.

gloss.crude: oil in its natural state, before it is refined
gloss.settle: to end a trading day at a certain price
gloss.benchmark: a standard price used to compare others
gloss.weekly gain: a rise in price over one week
gloss.liquefied petroleum gas: a fuel gas stored as a liquid, used for cooking and heating

items.title: Oil spill off UAE spreads
items.text: An oil spill off the coast of the United Arab Emirates has widened. It is now spreading towards Umm Al Quwain, one of the northern emirates. Authorities have closed more beaches as a result. Spills like this can harm wildlife and damage the local fishing and tourism industries. The cause of the spill was not given in the report, and officials have not said how long the clean-up will take.

gloss.spill: liquid that has accidentally flowed out of a container or ship
gloss.widen: to become larger or cover more area
gloss.emirate: one of the regions of the UAE, each ruled by an emir
gloss.close: to stop people from entering a place
